active_paradigms.idea: Replace the destination-only Steiner MILP with a partition-indexed capacitated broadcast MILP using scipy.optimize.milp
active_paradigms.description: The current program solves a binary directed-Steiner formulation: an activated edge is charged once and one binary commodity flow is created per distinct destination. This is strong when the evaluator charges the union of links, because it globally discovers shared prefixes rather than independently taking shortest paths. Its central blind spot is that it installs the identical route for every partition and never models aggregate edge flow, throughput, or partition-level overlap. Build one binary routing variable for each destination, partition, and directed edge, plus a binary edge-activation variable; retain source-to-destination conservation separately for every partition. Add an edge-capacity constraint whose left side is the number or volume of selected partition flows on that edge and whose right side is derived from its throughput, using the evaluator's implied partition demand/time convention. If completion time is scored, introduce a makespan variable and constrain each active edge's assigned traffic by throughput times that makespan; minimize evaluator-matching transfer cost plus an extremely small makespan tie-break. If cost is strictly union-of-links, preserve activation cost as the dominant objective but use capacity/makespan only as constraints or a lexicographic-scale secondary term. Extract each partition's selected path separately rather than replicating a destination path across all partitions.
active_paradigms.what_to_optimize: Primary transfer-cost score while preventing overloaded shared links and exploiting genuinely parallel partition routes; this directly addresses the current algorithm's complete non-use of num_partitions and throughput.
active_paradigms.cautions: The supplied wrapper exposes no metric computation beyond calling a hidden evaluator, so do not assume that cost is literally union-of-links without validating against evaluator behavior. Use integer/binary variables and scale throughput/demand coefficients to numerically stable values. Avoid charging an edge once per commodity if the evaluator charges it once per broadcast topology, and avoid charging it once globally if the evaluator instead charges each partition transfer. Enforce simple path extraction or remove cycles after solving, because zero-cost edges can otherwise create ambiguous selected flows. Keep a bounded solver time limit and preserve a feasible routing fallback if no incumbent is returned.

active_paradigms.idea: Use networkx.minimum_cost_flow as a throughput-aware partition assignment baseline when the evaluator charges actual transferred traffic
active_paradigms.description: The current Steiner solution is structurally optimized for shared edge activation, but it can be systematically wrong if the evaluator totals per-partition or per-byte path transfer cost. In that case, represent each partition-destination delivery as demand in an integer min-cost-flow network, with source supply equal to the number of required deliveries and destination demand equal to the number of partitions for that destination. Set each edge capacity from its usable throughput over the evaluator's transfer interval and set each edge weight to its per-unit monetary cost. A single networkx.minimum_cost_flow call then allocates deliveries across parallel routes globally instead of cloning every partition onto a single low-cost bottleneck. Convert the resulting positive-flow arcs into paths by decomposing flow from the source to each destination and assign those paths among partitions. This approach focuses on load balancing, so it is fundamentally different from selecting a minimum union-cost Steiner subgraph. It can outperform the current implementation particularly when throughput constraints or congestion penalties make using several slightly more expensive cloud links preferable to one cheap link.
active_paradigms.what_to_optimize: Aggregate per-transfer monetary cost and feasible parallel throughput, especially for scenarios where partition copies consume link capacity independently rather than receiving a free multicast on an activated edge.
active_paradigms.cautions: Do not use this as the final objective if tests confirm that an edge is paid only once regardless of how many partition paths traverse it; min-cost flow then deliberately overcounts sharing and the current Steiner principle is better. NetworkX demands must sum exactly to zero, capacities and weights should be finite integers, and all unreachable destinations must be handled explicitly before the call. Flow decomposition is required because a positive-flow subgraph is not itself a unique path per partition. If a destination appears repeatedly in dsts, aggregate its required demand but still populate every corresponding topology entry.

active_paradigms.idea: Use a rooted minimum arborescence via networkx.minimum_spanning_arborescence to enforce a clean shared broadcast tree
active_paradigms.description: The present MILP allows different commodity paths to merge and diverge arbitrarily, and its extraction phase can discard activated structure that was useful only indirectly; it also pays substantial solve overhead for small cloud graphs. Construct a source-rooted directed graph by deleting incoming source edges, invalid-cost edges, and vertices that cannot reach any required destination, then run networkx.minimum_spanning_arborescence with cost as the edge weight. The resulting branching gives every retained node exactly one incoming parent and therefore produces unambiguous, cycle-free source-to-destination paths with maximal prefix sharing. Prune leaves that are not destinations after the arborescence call, and install each destination's unique root path for its partitions. This is a different structural hypothesis from both unrestricted Steiner optimization and traffic flow: it asserts that a broadcast should be a replication tree, which often matches cloud multicast accounting and prevents redundant reconvergent transfers. It is especially attractive if hidden validation favors a single coherent broadcast topology, or if solver timeouts currently trigger the much weaker greedy fallback.
active_paradigms.what_to_optimize: Union-of-link broadcast cost, deterministic feasibility, and elimination of redundant cycles or multiple incompatible parent routes; it is a robust fast alternative when exact MILP incumbents are unavailable.
active_paradigms.cautions: A minimum arborescence spans every node left in the graph, so aggressively restrict the graph to source-reachable nodes that can reach at least one destination before the call; otherwise it can buy irrelevant edges. Standard arborescence is not an exact directed-Steiner solver because mandatory nonterminal nodes influence the result, so it should be benchmarked as an alternative rather than blindly combined with the MILP. Ensure every terminal is reachable after pruning and retain only finite nonnegative costs. If throughput is a hard requirement, remove infeasible edges before forming the arborescence or use this only where capacities are nonbinding.

tried_paradigms.idea: Replace the size-limited Steiner DP and greedy fallback with an exact directed Steiner arborescence MILP using scipy.optimize.milp
tried_paradigms.description: The current program minimizes a union-of-edges cost with an exact subset DP only when there are at most nine unique non-source destinations, then switches to a myopic least-marginal-cost attachment heuristic. Its main strength is that it correctly recognizes that identical partition routes should share a broadcast tree rather than independently paying for source-to-destination shortest paths. Its weakness is the abrupt loss of global optimality for larger destination sets, plus the DP cannot incorporate throughput, capacity, or route-selection constraints. Build a binary edge-activation variable for every usable directed edge and a binary per-terminal commodity variable for each edge, with commodity flow-conservation constraints from src to each destination and constraints commodity_use[e,t] <= activated_edge[e]. Minimize the activated-edge cost, optionally adding a very small deterministic tie-break term based on inverse throughput or hop count so equal-cost trees favor robust links. Use scipy.optimize.milp with integrality on both activation and commodity variables, bounds of [0,1], and sparse scipy LinearConstraint matrices. Extract activated edges, prune non-terminal dead branches, and derive each destination route from the resulting rooted arborescence before assigning it to every partition. This directly solves the same shared-transfer objective assumed by the current successful program for arbitrary destination counts, rather than relying on an uncontrolled fallback.
tried_paradigms.what_to_optimize: Primary shared broadcast transfer cost: minimize the cost of the unique directed links used by the multicast topology, especially for requests with more than nine destinations where the current greedy fallback can be arbitrarily suboptimal.
tried_paradigms.cautions: The evaluator source shown is only a wrapper, so confirm whether it charges unique broadcast links or charges every partition traversal; this MILP is appropriate for the former semantics. Remove null-cost edges and incoming edges to src as the current implementation does. Add only terminals reachable from src, use a solver time limit, and retain a feasible incumbent/fallback if the MILP terminates early. Do not model each partition as an independent commodity unless evaluator cost actually scales by partition, because that destroys the broadcast-sharing benefit.

tried_paradigms.idea: Use networkx.shortest_simple_paths to make partitions genuinely parallel and congestion-aware instead of cloning one tree route onto every partition
tried_paradigms.description: The current program writes exactly the same route for every partition of a destination, so all partitions contend on every shared link even though make_nx_graph provides throughput values specifically suitable for detecting bottlenecks. Preserve a low-cost shared tree or shortest base route as a reference, but call networkx.shortest_simple_paths on a weight that combines monetary cost with a small throughput-sensitive penalty to enumerate a bounded set of loop-free alternatives for each destination. For each destination-partition pair, choose from the first k candidates by minimum projected completion contribution, where adding a partition increases the load estimate on every edge in that candidate. Keep a route on the common cheap prefix when it is beneficial, but divert later partitions at congested relay nodes onto alternatives with spare throughput. The selection criterion should be lexicographic: avoid any edge whose projected flow exceeds throughput first, then minimize incremental monetary edge cost, then minimize latency/hops as a tie-breaker. This is fundamentally different from the current static Steiner construction because the topology is now partition-specific and can exploit overlapping transfers only where overlap remains physically feasible. It is particularly promising if the hidden scorer accounts for aggregate flow, makespan, overloaded links, or penalizes failed capacity constraints in addition to link prices.
tried_paradigms.what_to_optimize: Throughput feasibility, transfer completion time, and load balance across parallel network routes while retaining as much low-cost shared-prefix structure as possible.
tried_paradigms.cautions: Do not blindly assign distinct alternatives: if the evaluator prices a used edge only once and ignores throughput, unnecessary divergence increases union cost. Enumerate only a small k and stop the generator promptly to avoid exponential simple-path enumeration. Edge attributes may have missing or zero throughput, so treat them as unusable or impose a very large penalty. Every selected candidate must be converted to the required [[u, v, G[u][v]]] edge-list format and must be a valid src-to-dst directed route.

tried_paradigms.idea: Use networkx.network_simplex as a capacitated min-cost-flow formulation when evaluator charges actual partition traffic rather than only activated tree edges
tried_paradigms.description: A key unverified assumption in the current program is that all partitions sent over the same edge are charged once as a broadcast; however, the graph also exposes throughput and flow fields, which may mean the scorer instead sums traffic-dependent transfer cost and enforces capacity. In that model, the current reuse of one route for all partitions can be poor because it creates concentrated flow and ignores capacity entirely. Create a flow graph with source demand equal to negative total partition demand, each destination demand equal to its requested number of partitions, and zero demand at relays. Give every original edge a capacity derived from throughput under the evaluator's partition-time convention and a weight equal to per-partition transfer price, optionally with integer-scaled costs because network_simplex is most reliable with integral weights. Call networkx.network_simplex to find a globally capacity-feasible minimum-cost allocation, then decompose its positive integral edge flows into src-to-destination path units and assign those units to partition indices. Shared prefixes naturally carry aggregated flow, while branch links carry only traffic required by their respective destinations. This replaces the current tree heuristic with a globally coupled optimization of all destinations and partitions, which is the right abstraction if the evaluator independently aggregates traffic over edges.
tried_paradigms.what_to_optimize: Total traffic-priced transfer cost under edge-throughput constraints, avoiding overload penalties and balancing partition flows across available networks.
tried_paradigms.cautions: Ordinary min-cost flow cannot represent free multicast replication: it charges an edge once per unit of flow. Therefore use this only if inspection/testing establishes that the evaluator sums partition traffic or uses edge flow/capacity, rather than charging a broadcast edge once. Network simplex requires a balanced demand total and finite integer capacities; scale fractional throughput and costs consistently. Flow decomposition must handle cycles by removing circulation before extracting paths, and unreachable destination demand should trigger the existing shortest-path-safe fallback rather than returning incomplete paths.
